request.spec:
A retired person can be unretired (a button on the row; PERSON_UNRETIRED name=<name> on=<the
sheet's today>; anyone not retired is refused with an error on the row). They are no longer retired
(retired no, no retired-from); the retirement is kept on the row as <from> to <the day unretired>, one line per past
retirement; and a claim dated after the from and before the to of a
past retirement is refused as a claim after a retirement is.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A retired person can be unretired (a button on the row; PERSON_UNRETIRED name=<name> on=<the
sheet's today>; anyone not retired is refused with an error on the row). They are no longer retired
(retired no, no retired-from); the retirement is kept on the row as <from> to <the day unretired>, one line per past
retirement; and a claim dated after the from and before the to of a
past retirement is refused as a claim after a retirement is.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've added unretire, and `bin/e2e` passes: all 4 tests in the spec (the main "unretire" test and scenarios 1–3).

**How it works**
- **Button and refusal:** each person's row now has an Unretire button (`person-unretire`). Pressing it on someone who isn't retired shows the row's error (`person-error`) and changes nothing. On a retired person it clears their retirement, so the row shows `retired` no and an empty retired-from.
- **Audit:** it writes `PERSON_UNRETIRED sheet=… by=… name=… on=<sheet's today>`, followed by the usual ROLLUP/TOTALS lines when the person's figures change. That happens because their claims count in the totals again once they're no longer retired.
- **Past retirements on the row:** each ended retirement shows as a `person-retirement-line` reading `<from> to <day unretired>`, one per retirement, oldest first.
- **Claim refusal:** a claim dated strictly after the from and strictly before the to of a past retirement is refused, the same way a claim after a current retirement is. Dates on either boundary are allowed, which is what the test expects. Every path that already checks retirement (adding, editing, re-dating and reassigning claims) picks this up.

**Storage**
- **New column:** a migration (`V70__person_past_retirements.sql`) adds a `past_retirements` column to the person table, holding `from:to` pairs. It also adds the column to the as-of history copies of that table.
- **Why a column:** I chose it over a separate table so the as-of history and the existing person reads cover it with no extra work. The tradeoff is that past retirements aren't carried over when a person is transferred or merged, the same as holds today.

**Other changes**
- **New endpoint:** `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/unretire`, built the same way as the existing retire endpoint.
- **Wording change:** when a claim is refused because of a retirement, the claim form and claim editor now show the server's message instead of building their own text. That's because the old text quoted the current retirement date, and a person refused for a past retirement no longer has one.

**Edge case:** if someone is retired from a future date and unretired before that date arrives, their past-retirement line will run backwards (the "to" earlier than the "from"). Such a period covers no dates, so it never refuses a claim, but it reads oddly. The request doesn't cover this case and I left it as is.
